chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
A woman is not to be appointed as the executor entrusted with a bequest, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
And do not give the weak-minded your wealth.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Commander of the Faithful, Imam ʿAli عليه السلام
key_terms.أَمْوَالَكُمْ: your wealth or property entrusted for management
key_terms.اَلسَّكُونِيُّ: Al-Sakuni, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.اَلسُّفَهَاءَ: those considered lacking sound judgment in managing property
key_terms.اَلْمَرْأَةُ: a woman, the subject of the legal ruling in the report
key_terms.يُوصَى: to be appointed over a bequest or made executor

ai.seo_question: Can a woman be appointed as an executor of a will according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning the appointment of an executor for a bequest, grounding it in a Qur'anic expression about withholding wealth from those deemed incapable of proper management. It reflects a juridical use of Qur'anic wording in deriving rulings related to financial responsibility and entrusted authority.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5533 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said that the Commander of the Faithful (as) said:
"A woman should not be appointed as an executor of a will because Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, says: "
And do not give the weak-minded your wealth" (Surah An-Nisa 4:5)."
